label: improve_validation
source_context: Shumway documents biases when large negative delisting returns go unobserved.
scenario: A signal study uses a historical universe that includes vanished issuers and stores each feature as it was known. The forward-return function silently discards any name without a closing quote at horizon end. Some were removed after insolvency. The portfolio weights and measured transaction costs are sound for positions with complete returns. The main result depends on what happened to all positions that were opened, including those that never received an ordinary closing quote.
rationale: Dropping incomplete position outcomes selects which investments count after the decision date. Reconstruct delisting and liquidation returns and rerun the evaluation on the original portfolio.

label: audit_timing
source_context: The Philadelphia Fed maintains historical snapshots of reported macroeconomic series.
scenario: A quarterly allocation study reports that economic contractions were detected promptly. The matrix dates each value with the period it describes. Historical data are pulled in one query today, and the researchers have a parallel collection of historical releases that they have not joined. Price labels, portfolio risk and market impact are already measured on eligible orders.
rationale: The feature matrix needs historical eligibility and the original reported values.

label: improve_validation
source_context: Novy-Marx studies how screening and combining candidate signals affect backtest significance.
scenario: The desk combined two characteristics after visiting rankings for 600 candidate pairs. Its analyst reports a t-statistic for the winner using every month, including the months displayed in the rankings. Other groups sourced the feature histories correctly and verified fees. A separate, untouched slice will become available next quarter.
rationale: The evaluation should account for selection and preserve a truly independent confirmation set.

label: model_costs
source_context: Frazzini, Israel and Moskowitz study realized trading costs and capacity across styles.
scenario: A monthly equity strategy passed a time-sealed evaluation. The execution team measured fills for small orders. The portfolio expansion would need several times the order size and increasingly trade names with less displayed depth. A governance review verified exposures and downside limits for the larger weights. The reported net return still applies the small-order conversion from target weight to cost.
rationale: The size-sensitive relationship between order size and execution loss is needed before treating small-order evidence as scalable.

label: limit_risk
source_context: Brunnermeier, Nagel and Pedersen examine downside risk and unwinds in currency carry.
scenario: A diversified-looking style held many bilateral positions. Its test already incorporates ordinary costs, valid decisions and exposure to the chosen value signal. A joint stress replay leaves most positions losing on the same day when one funding leg strengthens, with the collateral requirement near a desk limit. Portfolio management has yet to decide how to cap this common exposure.
rationale: Stress exposes an unbounded shared funding exposure, so limit it before increasing the experiment.

label: clarify_thesis
source_context: McLean and Pontiff compare the evolution of stock-return predictor performance in and out of the original samples and after publication.
scenario: A team lists several explanations for a factor weakening after a research paper. Better arbitrage, a temporary economic regime and a biased published sample are all compatible with their story. Their independent historical archives support cohort analysis, and they have yet to state what pattern across publication cohorts would favor one mechanism over the others. They have not asked for allocation approval.
rationale: Specify discriminating predictions and what would falsify each mechanism before designing the cohort comparison.

label: model_costs
source_context: Lou, Polk and Skouras separate overnight and intraday return patterns.
scenario: A portfolio accrues most of its gross return between the official close and next open. Its signal is available before the close and passed a prospective paper test. However, the simulator books all entry and exit fills at a single indicative price even for large auction quantities. Historic order imbalance, auction prints and execution logs are available, but no one has reconstructed fills.
rationale: The priority is whether the marked return is executable after realistic auction fills and slippage.

label: run_pilot
source_context: Novy-Marx and Velikov evaluate anomaly performance with trading cost mitigation.
scenario: A portfolio rebalancing rule with a predeclared holding buffer passed independent chronological tests. An execution supervisor reconciled its orders against historical fills, including fees and conservative cost sensitivity. Position limits, stress loss and daily reconciliation have owners. The research log contains the exact stopping rule if live timestamps or execution costs drift. The only remaining uncertainty is whether the data and controls behave in a small monitored prospective run.
rationale: With prior decision gates documented, a capped prospective experiment directly addresses the unresolved operational uncertainty.
